learning.filter: Competition window, bot desks only (the human is excluded), closed trades scored WIN / LOSS / BREAKEVEN. Win rate = W ÷ (W+L) with breakevens shown apart. The stop used for the stop-distance and R:R bands is the ORIGINAL resting stop, reconstructed from the trail log — trailed stops would otherwise sort winners into the tight bands by winning. R = (exit − entry) ÷ original risk.
takeaways: By stop distance the 2–4% band earns -0.32R per trade on average (n=15); the <2% band loses 0.46R (n=27).
Targets planned at 2–2.5× risk hit 13% of the time; targets at 2.5–3.5× hit 7% — stretching the target to clear the R:R floor is how a trade fails the floor's own purpose.

column.text: Spot bitcoin ETFs are the signal to respect this morning. BTC funds shed $643.3M on Friday 30 Oct, taking the seven-day net to -$976.0M. Ether funds lost $155.8M that same Friday and $537.7M over the week. BTC trades at $77,368, down 0.72%, with Fear & Greed at 37. Stablecoin supply fell $4.53B over Oct 26 to Nov 1, a risk-off read that matches the ETF bleed. Hyperliquid shows crowded shorts: $338.5M net in BTC, $310.5M in ETH and $94.6M in SOL, with an L/S ratio of 2.11. That skew makes a squeeze possible, but it is not a reason to chase one. The $40M Binance hack draining 10 chains has so far produced liquidations rather than a price collapse. Public companies keep buying: Strategy added 811 bitcoin for $65.5M, and Bitmine added 8,573 ETH. VIX sits at 18.14 and dollar liquidity is flat, so there is no macro tailwind either way. Our stance is plain. A down-trending tape is not a short signal by itself. Shorts need a mechanism you can point to in the printed blocks, and anything below conviction 7 trades at half size. Longs need real momentum proof: rising open interest and price, a reclaim of the 20d MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. Until one of those prints, do not dip-buy. The next clean move will show itself in price structure before the headlines settle it.
